paths.description: Homepage/start-page archetype and primary search entry; tested visual preferences, metadata, crawler HTML, performance, security, keyboard focus, and memory.
Primary search journey and results/failure archetype using query “web uplift”; tested desktop/mobile completion and recovery.
Unknown-route/error recovery archetype; redirects to Yahoo portal and displayed a reversible consent dialog.

findings.summary: The page ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: Dark-emulated and light screenshots are pixel-equivalent in the page surface; computed html background stays rgb(255,255,255) and color-scheme is normal.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and provide preference-driven surface, text, border, icon, and form colors using prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Search navigation swaps documents abruptly without a view transition.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection found no view-transition usage, and the home-to-results journey performs a plain full navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Add progressive cross-document View Transitions for the persistent logo/search field, with reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Overlay implementations use custom role=dialog containers rather than native dialog/popover primitives.
findings.evidence: Structure probe found three DIV elements with role=dialog and no dialog or popover element.
findings.suggestedFix: Migrate modal flows to <dialog> and transient UI to popover, preserving accessible naming and declarative light-dismiss.

findings.summary: Search results ship a fixed desktop canvas on a narrow phone viewport.
findings.evidence: At 360x800, results layout measured scrollWidth 1280 versus clientWidth 360 (920 px overflow); the screenshot clips the failure text and all right-side controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace fixed widths/offsets with intrinsic fluid layout and container queries; verify every results module at 320–400 CSS px without horizontal overflow.

findings.summary: Key controls are too small and the primary input removes keyboard focus indication.
findings.evidence: Focus probe measured 20x20 voice/settings controls, 24x24 stop control, and the search input outline as none; several results controls also set outline:0.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide at least 44x44 touch hit areas and a high-contrast :focus-visible style for every control, especially the query input and icon buttons.

findings.summary: The primary search task did not complete.
findings.evidence: Submitting the representative query “web uplift” repeatedly returned “We had temporary problems searching for web pages” instead of results on desktop and mobile.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix or fail over the search backend, add operational monitoring, and preserve a useful alternate result path while the primary provider is unavailable.

findings.summary: Cold mobile loading misses the good LCP range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 7.7 s, FCP 2.3 s, Speed Index 5.0 s, and performance 0.69; a separate trace measured LCP 1.80 s, showing substantial run variability.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP request chain under mobile throttling, reduce document latency, preload only the actual LCP dependency, and defer consent/analytics work.

findings.summary: Render-blocking and cache/font delivery delay first content.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 1,080 ms render-blocking savings and flags inefficient cache lifetimes, font display, and dependency chains; HAR shows a parser stylesheet at VeryHigh priority.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline minimal critical CSS, defer non-critical assets, use font-display with metric-compatible fallback, and set durable immutable caching for versioned resources.

findings.summary: The compact homepage ships substantial unused code.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 189 KiB unused JavaScript and 39 KiB unused CSS, plus legacy JavaScript; HAR transfers 687 KiB script for a small search page.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split voice, consent, and secondary modules; load on intent; remove unused CSS and avoid legacy transforms for Baseline browsers.

findings.summary: Some links lack discernible accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility score was 0.82 and the link-name audit failed; the DOM contains icon-only links including a mail anchor with empty text.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every icon link an aria-label or visible name and verify the accessibility tree for all interactive elements.

findings.summary: Document structure and keyboard order are not robust.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed heading-order, one-main-landmark, listitem, and positive-tabindex audits; structure probe found no main and starts visible headings at H3.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a main landmark, use a logical H1→H2 hierarchy and valid lists, remove positive tabindex, and preserve DOM reading order.

findings.summary: Zoom and reflow are restricted and mobile results do not reflow.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports a viewport that disables/restricts scaling; home layout has no viewport meta in one served variant, while results overflow by 920 px at 360 px.
findings.suggestedFix: Use width=device-width, initial-scale=1 without maximum-scale/user-scalable restrictions, then test 200–400% zoom and 320 px reflow.

findings.evidence: Lighthouse’s “Browser errors were logged to the console” audit scored 0.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve the recorded runtime/network errors and add production error monitoring that catches regressions without leaking user queries.

findings.summary: Large first-party scripts lack valid source maps.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed valid-source-maps for large first-party JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish correct, access-controlled production source maps or remove invalid sourceMappingURL references.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced security is incomplete and two cookies are not Secure.
findings.evidence: Headers primitive found no CSP or Permissions-Policy; cookies primitive found sBS and _dmit without Secure, and SameSite=None cookies. HSTS, nosniff, and DENY framing are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP and restrictive Permissions-Policy; mark all HTTPS cookies Secure and tighten SameSite/HttpOnly according to actual use.

findings.summary: Third-party tracking and consent code dominate the lightweight search page.
findings.evidence: Trackers found four third-party origins including Google Tag Manager; HAR attributes 1.366 MB of 1.414 MB transferred to third parties. The generic consent.js API-key pattern was not treated as a secret because context indicates public consent configuration.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate analytics on consent, minimize query-adjacent telemetry, self-host where justified, batch events, and document retention/purpose.

findings.summary: The localized page relies extensively on physical positioning.
findings.evidence: The document correctly declares lang=en-IN, but captured CSS repeatedly uses left/right offsets, margins, borders, and floats; no dir-aware logical-property strategy was visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Use margin/padding/inset-inline and block logical properties, set dir where needed, and test an RTL locale before reuse.

findings.summary: The page transfers 1.4 MB largely for non-core media and third-party code.
findings.evidence: HAR transfers 1,414,038 bytes: 505,520 bytes of four voice audio files before voice use, 687,209 bytes of script, and 1,365,731 third-party bytes; voice audio alone includes 190 KB and 150 KB files.
findings.suggestedFix: Load voice audio and implementation only after user intent, reduce consent/analytics payloads, reuse system effects where possible, and set a purpose-appropriate page-weight budget.
